entries.text: Talked about starting a new medication with the psychiatrist and how sleep has been. They noticed they feel calmer when they keep a routine.
They kept the evening routine: tea, reading, no phone. Fell asleep calmer.
Missed the routine on Friday and felt wired. Came back to it on Saturday.
The routine holds most nights now. They feel steadier.

theme: long backfill, many notes on overwhelm

expect.note: More than 15 entries: needs two jobs before the first read is done.

entries.text: Too many things at once: work launch, sick kid, moving flat. They cried in the car.
They wrote a list and picked one thing for the day. Felt slightly lighter.
Asked their partner to take the school runs this week. They said yes.
Overwhelmed again at work. Took a five minute walk before answering emails.
They said no to a new committee at work. It felt good.
Bad day. Snapped at the kids. Later apologised.
Picked one thing again, finished it, stopped there.
Took the five minute walk before a hard meeting.
Asked a friend to help pack boxes. They came with pizza.
The move happened. Exhausted but proud of how they handled it.
They noticed overwhelm starts when they try to do everything perfectly.
Left some laundry undone on purpose. Rested instead.
Five minute walk again, this time after a fight with their manager.
One thing a day still works. Today it was the tax form.
Asked for an extension on a deadline. Got it.
Calm weekend in the new flat. Read a book in the sun.
They noticed they now ask for help sooner.
Overwhelm came back with the school concert week. Wrote the list, picked one thing.
They turned down a second project and felt no guilt this time.
Quiet week. They feel steadier than in spring.

skills.name: Noticing what sets it off
skills.in_your_words: You notice when overwhelm starts, like when you try to do everything perfectly. You can also see it in the car or when too many things pile up at once.

skills.name: Picking one thing
skills.in_your_words: You choose one thing for the day, finish it, and stop there. That helps when work, family, and moving all land on you at once.

skills.name: Asking for help
skills.in_your_words: You ask the people around you to take some of the load, like school runs or packing boxes. You do not carry all of it alone.

skills.name: Choosing one thing
skills.in_your_words: You write a list, pick one thing, and do that. That can help you keep the day simple when there is a lot around you.

skills.name: Resting without doing it all
skills.in_your_words: You leave some things undone and rest instead. You also read in the sun, which seems to help you feel a bit lighter.

skills.name: Settling back down
skills.in_your_words: You notice when things feel lighter or steadier, and you give yourself a small pause to let that land. You also let some things stay undone so you can rest.

skills.name: Doing one thing
skills.in_your_words: You pick one thing for the day and stop there. Sometimes it is the tax form, sometimes it is a list that helps you choose.

theme: fear of driving after an accident

entries.text: Talked about the small accident last winter. They noticed their hands sweat when they even think about driving on the motorway.
Drove to the shop on quiet streets with a friend in the car. Breathed out slowly at each light.
Drove alone to work on the back roads. Scared but did it.
Still avoided the motorway when a colleague offered the faster route. That is still hard.
Drove to their parents, back roads, slow breathing at the lights. Felt almost normal.

entries.text: Napisała, że przed prezentacją w pracy cała się trzęsła i bała się, że szef ją oceni. Prawie odwołała spotkanie.
Sesja o lęku przed oceną. Zauważyła, że najgorsze są pierwsze minuty. Terapeutka zaproponowała, żeby na początku powiedzieć jedno zdanie o tym, jak się czuje.
Na spotkaniu zespołu powiedziała, że trochę się stresuje, i od razu zrobiło się lżej. Poprowadziła prezentację do końca.
Zgłosiła się do prowadzenia kolejnego spotkania. Bała się, ale była dumna.
Odpowiedziała szefowi wprost, że potrzebuje więcej czasu na raport. Wciąż trudno jej mówić to na głos przy wszystkich.

entries.text: Three months since their father died. They keep picking up the phone to call him.
Session on grief. They noticed they push sadness away by staying busy. Their therapist suggested letting a wave come and pass without fixing it.
Looked at old photos and let themselves cry for a while. Afterwards felt lighter.
Talked about the funeral and what they never said. Wrote a letter to their father in the app.
Told their brother they miss dad. They talked for an hour, the first real talk in years.
His birthday. Hard day. They let the sadness come and went for a walk to his favourite bench.
